description.short_caption: Comparison of normal urine (left) and abnormal cloudy urine (right).
description.detailed_description: The image shows two transparent cups placed side by side on a blue cloth background. The cup on the left contains clear, yellow-colored urine, consistent with normal appearance. The cup on the right contains cloudy, pale, and turbid urine, suggesting the presence of abnormalities such as infection, proteinuria, or pyuria. The contrast between the two samples is visually striking.
visible_findings: clear yellow urine in left cup
cloudy, pale, turbid urine in right cup
contrast in clarity and color between the two samples

description.short_caption: Blood smear showing a microfilaria among red blood cells.
description.detailed_description: This image is a stained blood smear showing a microfilaria, a parasitic nematode, surrounded by numerous red blood cells. The microfilaria is elongated, with a coiled and segmented appearance, and is significantly larger than the surrounding erythrocytes. The staining highlights the internal structures of the parasite and provides contrast against the background cells. The smear is likely stained with a technique such as Giemsa or Wright stain, commonly used for identifying blood parasites.
visible_findings: numerous red blood cells in the background

description.short_caption: Axial abdominal CT scan showing bowel loops and intra-abdominal structures.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT scan of the abdomen shows multiple loops of bowel, some of which appear distended with gas and fluid. The vertebral body is visible in the center, and surrounding soft tissues and intra-abdominal structures are present. There is a large, rounded, hypodense area in the left side of the image, suggestive of a fluid-filled or cystic structure. The scan is without contrast, as no enhancement is visible.
visible_findings: hypodense rounded structure in the left abdomen
